claims.statement: This GCP guide covers FPT/GHEC/GHES and describes federation through google-github-actions/auth without long-lived GCP secrets; GHES lacks hosted runners.
OIDC prerequisites require at least one trust condition excluding untrusted repositories. Dependabot dynamic event_name is feature-gated to FPT/GHEC/GHES>3.20; GHE.com substitutions are GHEC-only.

The GCP guide includes repositories created after July15,2026 and repositories renamed/transferred after that date in immutable owner/repository-ID subjects, excludes GHES, and says existing repositories retain old format unless opted in.
GHES discovery/JWKS endpoints must be accessible; GCP has no fixed IP ranges and the JWT issuer must be publicly routable.
The prescribed GCP setup creates an identity pool, maps claims/adds conditions and connects it to a service account; no resource creation is performed here.

Review cloud trust; the source requires roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser for service-account configuration and selects public versus GHES issuer URLs. Exact role bindings and effective resource permissions remain unverified.
The workflow needs OIDC issuance permission and an auth action to exchange the JWT; environments warrant recommended protection rules.
The identity-provider resource path and service account are example substitutions for workload identity federation, not actual admitted identities.

The sample triggers pull requests targeting main, uses a patterned full-SHA-shaped auth reference and creates a credential file; syntax does not prove action origin, trusted triggering inputs or safe credential-file handling.
The sample logs in gcloud using the emitted credential-file path and lists services; credential secrecy and actual cloud access need separate evidence.
The third-party action comment disclaims GitHub certification and preserves separate terms/privacy/support.
Further reading remains navigation outside whole-file certification.

scope: Full pinned article and literal closure read; source propositions are reference-only and do not adopt policy.
